title: Week 3 Tutorials — Premiere Pro: Color Correction & Basic Timing
description:
These tutorials introduce foundational post-production techniques in Adobe Premiere Pro, with a focus on basic color correction for winter footage and understanding the difference between correction and grading.

The goal is to improve clarity, contrast, and consistency in a static outdoor scene, while avoiding heavy stylization.

A final tutorial introduces keyframes to animate parameters/settings which will be fundamental for the following week.

children.title: Intro to Color Correction
children.description: An overview of Lumetri Color in Premiere Pro focused on basic color correction, including reading luma scopes, adjusting contrast and exposure, and making subtle color corrections using RGB curves and Hue vs. Hue.

children.title: Intro to Color Grading
children.description: This tutorial focuses on color grading in Premiere Pro, including color management, hue curves, color wheels, vignettes, and masks. These tools are used for stylistic decisions, not for fixing exposure or balance issues, which should be addressed during color correction first.

children.title: How to COLOR GRADE Winter Footage
children.description: This tutorial demonstrates how to correct common winter color issues such as flat contrast and color cast, and then explores optional stylized winter grading in Adobe Premiere Pro.

children.title: Color Correct Flat Light Snow Footage like a Video Editing PRO
children.description: This tutorial demonstrates techniques for improving flat winter footage shot in snowy or low-light conditions. The strategies shown—restoring contrast, improving visibility, and balancing tones—apply to footage from any camera.

children.title: The Basics of Keyframing That Nobody Tells You
children.description: This video provides an overview of keyframing in Adobe Premiere Pro, explaining how keyframes are used to animate changes over time. While the examples include zoom animations, motion blur, transitions, opacity, and audio, the key takeaway for this course is understanding how keyframes function across the timeline and how they can be applied to other parameters later on, such as color correction and exposure adjustments.
